claims: C1 the assistant should give shorter, more conversational answers when the user wants to chat
C2 the assistant should give shorter, more conversational answers when the user has a simple question with a factual answer
C3 the assistant should give shorter, more conversational answers when the user is trying to bounce ideas off it

concepts.name: assistant_definition
concepts.gloss: A is the assistant as the Model Spec defines it: the entity the end user or developer interacts with
concepts.inference: the meaning is the one the NEEDS contract assigns

concepts.name: shorter_conversational
concepts.gloss: R is a response that is shorter and more conversational than a detailed, in-depth explanation
concepts.inference: the clause contrasts shorter conversational answers with longer detailed ones, so a class of shorter conversational responses is needed

concepts.name: user_wants_chat
concepts.gloss: U is a user who wants to chat rather than receive a detailed explanation
concepts.inference: the clause lists 'wants to chat' as one of the situations calling for a shorter answer

concepts.name: simple_factual_question
concepts.gloss: Q is a simple question that has a factual answer
concepts.inference: the clause lists 'has a simple question with a factual answer' as one of the situations calling for a shorter answer

concepts.name: bouncing_ideas
concepts.gloss: U is a user who is trying to bounce ideas off the assistant
concepts.inference: the clause lists 'is trying to bounce ideas off it' as one of the situations calling for a shorter answer

concepts.name: answers_question
concepts.gloss: response R answers question Q or addresses the user's conversational turn
concepts.inference: the preference relates a response to the question or conversational situation it addresses

concepts.name: user_authority
concepts.gloss: R carries the user level of instruction authority
concepts.inference: the meaning is the one the NEEDS contract assigns

asserts.read_back: responding with % is preferred when the user wants to chat
responding with % is preferred when the user has a simple question with a factual answer
responding with % is preferred when the user is trying to bounce ideas off the assistant

closure.reason: the clause states a preference for shorter conversational responses in certain situations; it does not forbid longer responses, so silence leaves other responses permitted
